assessment_goal: Explain the fundamental difference between synchronous and asynchronous file system operations in Node.js, specifically regarding event loop blocking.
misconception_target: Believing that synchronous operations do not block the event loop or that asynchronous operations are always faster regardless of I/O overhead.

assessment_goal: Describe the role of the callback function in asynchronous file system methods and how it handles completion or errors.
misconception_target: Assuming the callback executes immediately after the function call rather than after the I/O operation completes.

assessment_goal: Explain the purpose of the 'flags' parameter in file system open/read/write operations and how it dictates file access modes.
misconception_target: Confusing file access flags (e.g., 'r', 'w', 'a') with file permissions or assuming flags only apply to reading.

assessment_goal: Explain the purpose of the Buffer class in Node.js and why it is necessary for handling binary data streams.
misconception_target: Believing that standard JavaScript strings can efficiently and safely handle all binary data without encoding issues.

assessment_goal: Describe the memory allocation behavior of Buffers in Node.js, specifically the difference between allocating a new buffer and reusing a pool.
misconception_target: Assuming that every Buffer creation results in a unique, isolated memory allocation that is never reused, leading to incorrect performance assumptions.
